title: Most Words in One Sentence
statement:
You get a list of strings sentences. Each sentence is made of lowercase words separated by exactly one space, with no space at the start or the end.

Return the largest number of words found in any single sentence.

examples.why: The three sentences have 2, 4 and 1 words.
Count words, not characters. The single long word is one word.
A sentence with no spaces still has one word.

constraints: Words are lowercase English letters, separated by single spaces

args: one two three four five six
a b c d e f g h i j

hints: How does the number of words in one sentence relate to something easy to count?
With single spaces and no spaces at the ends, a sentence with k spaces has exactly k + 1 words.
Count spaces (or split on a space) for each sentence and keep the maximum.

explain.intuition:
The input is clean: one space between words, none at the ends. So every space separates two words, and a sentence with k spaces has k + 1 words. Count that per sentence and keep the largest.

split(" ") gives the same number and reads naturally, at the cost of building an array for every sentence. Counting spaces does no allocation, which is the habit you want when the same code runs over a big text in the browser.
steps: For each sentence, count its spaces and add 1.
pitfalls: Picking the longest sentence by character count. A long single word beats several short words on characters but not on words.
Counting spaces without adding 1, which reports 0 for a one-word sentence.
Using split(" ") on messy input with double spaces would count empty strings as words. Here the input rules this out, but say so if you rely on it.

solutions.title: Split each sentence
solutions.idea: Split on a single space and take the longest resulting list.

solutions.title: Count spaces
solutions.idea: Words are spaces plus one, because each space sits between two words.

followups: Sentences may now have leading, trailing and repeated spaces. How do you count words correctly without building arrays?
Return the index of the wordiest sentence, choosing the earliest on ties.
